takeaways.label: 5th straight quarter of double-digit growth
takeaways.text: Revenue and profit hit all-time highs, with management upgrading the full-year growth target to 20%+ and guiding for EBITDA to grow more than 50% in H2.

takeaways.label: US base-effect masks stabilization
takeaways.text: A one-off exclusivity launch in Q2 FY26 (₹0.5 cr at 90%+ margin) makes the YoY comparison look like a decline, but the underlying business has stabilized at a ₹100-115 cr quarterly run rate with no further downside expected.

takeaways.label: The strategy is now a multi-year investment cycle
takeaways.text: The company is shifting from mature-product launches to day-one generic launches, requiring a step-up in R&D (₹40 cr animal health, up from ₹10-12 cr) and a dedicated companion animal facility, which is why EBITDA margins are not expanding despite top-line growth.

takeaways.label: Balance sheet is rapidly deleveraging
takeaways.text: Net debt fell from ₹166 cr to ₹26 cr in six months on strong operating cash flow of ₹182 cr, even as ESOP expenses jumped from ₹26 cr to ₹67 cr due to amalgamation grants.

watch.label: What to watch next quarter
watch.text: Whether the Bio4Life acquisition starts contributing, the pace of API recovery after a war-disrupted H1, and any concrete acquisition announcement given management's signal that next year could be the peak year for deals.

points.label: The Q2 FY26 one-off
points.text: An exclusive CZT product launch generated ~₹0.5 cr top line at 90%+ gross margin, but API supplier delays meant only ~1.5 months of the 6-month exclusivity window was utilized. That elevated base makes Q2 FY27 appear as a decline.

points.label: Post-exclusivity reality
points.text: Other approvals came in from Q3 FY26 onward, and the company maintained ~50% gross market share. The business has since stabilized at a ₹100-115 cr quarterly run rate, and management sees no further downside.

points.label: FY27 US growth commitment
points.text: Confident of 10% growth for the full year even without major new launches, and "close to" 15%+ is possible. One big exclusive launch (sole filer, ~$90 mn product, API patent expired, formulation patent circumvented, no litigation) is expected next year and could be significant if day-one exclusivity materializes.

points.label: US generics penetration today
points.text: Volume is ~80% generic but value is only 15-20%, because brands command 80% of value on 20% of volume. Management expects this to shift quickly after 3-4 years as more blockbusters lose exclusivity.

quotes.text: Dr. Haribabu: "We could able to utilize that opportunity one of-- one and a half month in Q2 FY26, which generated almost 0.5 crore revenue top line and 90% plus gross margin. That changes actually the numbers both top line and bottom line for the US business."

points.label: The strategy pivot
points.text: The entire company strategy has shifted from launching mature products to launching day-one generics post-patent expiry. This requires a longer gestation period and sizable upfront investment, which is why EBITDA margins are not growing: the company is investing for the future.

points.label: The blockbuster opportunity
points.text: Three major products with combined brand value of ~$3 bn today (expected to grow to $3.5-4 bn by FY30) have patents expiring in February 2029. Viyash is targeting 10-15% market share even after 40-60% price erosion, with launches expected in FY30. In countries with local manufacturing (Brazil, Mexico, Turkey), launches can be advanced by 9-12 months.

points.label: Dedicated facility under construction
points.text: A new companion animal manufacturing facility in Ambarnath is expected to be ready by Q1 (Jan-Feb), with a 9-12 month approval cycle, making it comfortable for the FY29 launch timeline. The facility will have differentiated equipment for tablet size, flavors, and quality. A backup site in Turkey (via a Europe-approved partner) is also being filed in Dec-Jan.

points.label: Why own the facility
points.text: Management sees a fully integrated strategy as essential for differentiation, sustainability, and flexibility in the animal health business.

points.label: Current companion animal revenue
points.text: First half did close to ₹2 cr; full year expected close to ₹3 cr, ~60% growth off a low base.

points.label: Geographic expansion planned
points.text: Initial launches targeted at Europe, Brazil, Turkey, Mexico, India, and Southeast Asia, with extension to Australia, Canada, and other emerging markets 12-24 months after initial launches.

quotes.text: Dr. Haribabu: "It's our entire strategy is moving launching mature products to launching day one. That's the strategy we adopted after merger, but these, when you adopt these strategies, your gestation period is little high. We have to pick gestation period and also investments also sizable."

points.label: H1 disruption
points.text: The first half was hit by war-related raw material and solvent price spikes, plus customers on mature products minimizing inventory. Q1 was particularly low; Q2 rebounded to ~20% growth as procurement resumed.

points.label: H2 outlook
points.text: Second half is historically stronger for API, and management has strong visibility. Confident of at least 12-13% growth for the full year, with mid-teens possible if H2 delivers high-teens growth.

points.label: Animal health API
points.text: Tracking very well on 20%+ growth; albendazole capacity has been more than doubled and is working well. The base was low last year (~₹400 cr).

points.label: Human health API
points.text: New product approvals have been delayed; one iron complex product (big for both top line and bottom line) was anticipated in H1 but is now expected in H2. Overall, the year is tracking well despite quarter-to-quarter timing shifts.

points.label: Pipeline acceleration
points.text: Development capacity has expanded from 1-2 products annually for validation to 5-8 products annually, with most going for filing. One very big launch for Europe is expected next year, with continuous good launches from FY28 and FY29 onward.

points.label: FY28-29 guidance
points.text: On track for 13-15% growth, contingent on product launches materializing; if they do not, double-digit growth is still expected.

quotes.text: Dr. Haribabu: "Second half is going to be much better than first half, that I can tell you."

points.label: Q2 margin compression
points.text: EBITDA margin was 21.1% vs 22.1% YoY; gross margin was 53.7% vs 55.5% YoY. Three drivers: the high-margin US exclusivity product in the base quarter, raw material and solvent price spikes from the war (solvent impact alone ~0.3-0.4%), and product mix changes. Some price increases were passed but not all.

points.label: The investment trade-off
points.text: Animal health R&D has moved from ₹10-12 cr to ₹40 cr annually, and the company is building an oncology R&D center and a companion animal facility. Management is explicit that EBITDA margins are not growing because the company is investing for the future.

points.label: Gross margin normalization
points.text: Over the last 6-8 months, gross margins across API and formulation (especially animal health) have converged, varying only 2-3%. Management sees 54-55% as the right number for the next two years, with potential improvement as the mix shifts toward more complex products like oncology (FY29-30) and companion animal blockbusters (majority from FY29).

points.label: ESOP cost spike
points.text: ESOP expenses jumped from ₹26 cr in H1 FY26 to ₹67 cr in H1 FY27 due to incremental grants from the scheme of amalgamation. Normalization to ~₹25 cr per year is expected from Q1 FY28 onward.

points.label: R&D spend trajectory
points.text: FY27 full year: ~₹148-149 cr. Next year: ~₹32 cr (Q1: ~₹20 cr). Stable state thereafter: ~₹25 cr.

quotes.text: Dr. Haribabu: "I practically, I, I feel it's the right number, 54-55 gross margin."

points.label: Acquisition appetite is real
points.text: Management is actively exploring acquisitions, with a preference for front-end market access over manufacturing. The focus is on animal health, companion animal, specialty CDMO, and specialty product acquisitions (in-licensing or company acquisitions), not me-too or larger infrastructure plays.

points.label: Timing signal
points.text: "If not next 2 quarters, definitely we'll see next year," with next year potentially being the peak year for acquisitions. After that, the second year may focus on repaying debt and acquiring remaining minority stakes.

points.label: Bio4Life integration
points.text: The acquisition of Bio4Life Italy closed effective Oct 1, 2026, with consolidation from Q3 FY27. The first list of 10 products (gastro, dermatology, orthology) is being geo-extended to Europe, Brazil, LATAM, Turkey, and India, with benefits expected to start flowing in 2-3 years given 15-18 month registration timelines plus 6-8 months for marketing build.

points.label: Vietnam entry
points.text: Entity registration is complete, product registration has started, and commercial sales are expected from early next year, with $3-5 mn anticipated over the next couple of years.

points.label: Carlyle overhang
points.text: An ~11% block was recently sold to institutional buyers (Kotak, Mahindra, Edelweiss). Management's personal view is that no further exit is likely in the next 12-15 months, but they declined to speak for Carlyle's intentions.

quotes.text: Dr. Haribabu: "We don't want to acquire just for sake of numbers. That's the reason we are looking at the strategic fit into our strategy... Definitely you can see, uh, if not next 2 quarters, definitely we'll see next year."

points.label: Oncology R&D facility commissioned
points.text: A new finished-dosage R&D facility in Hyderabad can handle high-potent molecules up to OEB 5 level and is capable of pilot-scale batches.

points.label: Oncology strategy
points.text: Products will target Day 1 or Day 181 launches, with timing critical for Day 1 and efficiency critical for Day 181. Focus is on high-value products for the US market, with extension to Europe via partnerships. Material contribution is expected by FY29 or FY30.

points.label: Human health broader strategy
points.text: Continue moving from mature products to differentiated and complex products; transfer large-volume products to India for cost improvement; build a fully integrated oncology play spanning API, formulation, and front-end.

points.label: CDMO positioning
points.text: 90-95% of CDMO revenue is commercial, all from innovators with mature products. New CDMO contracts are with specialty pharma companies targeting launches 8-10 years out (2034-35). Managemen t acknowledged an unresolved question about how to manage potential conflicts with innovator CDMO partners as Viyash transitions to launching generics of blockbuster brands in the companion animal space.

items.title: Group revenue guidance
items.text: Management raised FY27 revenue growth guidance to 20%+ and targets $1 billion revenue by 2032, an 18% CAGR from the ~₹4,000 crore FY27 base, with 20-25% CAGR possible over the next 3-4 years. On FY26 revenue of ₹3,713 crore, 20% growth implies roughly ₹4,450 crore in FY27.

items.title: Companion animal platform
items.text: The BioForLife Italia acquisition (€16.975 million) completed 1 October 2026, adding ~85 products and a salesforce with ~85% vet-clinic coverage in Italy, with results consolidating from Q3 FY27; exclusive Boehringer Ingelheim India distribution began February 2026, covering parasiticides and vaccines addressing nearly two-thirds of the Indian companion animal market. Management targets "15 crore-20 crore" business scale by 2032, with major growth from FY29 day-1 launches against a ~$1.5 billion addressable market.

items.title: Companion animal launches and capacity
items.text: 29 day-1 launches are underway against patent expiries up to 2035, and 3-4 blockbuster products with basic patents expiring from calendar 2029 carry ~$3 billion of brand value today, where the company targets 10-15% share. The dedicated Ambarnath facility is commissioned by Q1 FY28, sized to meet FY29 launch requirements.

items.title: US exclusive launch FY28
items.text: The company is the only filer for a fully integrated, first-to-file product with a ~$90 million US market, launching in FY28 with a small litigation and limited API availability. A day-1 launch can capture 50-60% market share, on top of a US business guided to grow ~10% in FY27 toward ~₹480 crore.

items.title: CDMO lifecycle growth
items.text: The innovator life-cycle management business, on a ~₹200-225 crore base, is guided to grow 40% in FY27, with the wider innovator business up at least 30-40%. Sixteen to seventeen complex specialty-company products launch from 2029-30 through 2035-37, and a big Europe API/CMO launch lands next year.

items.title: API capacity and growth
items.text: FY27 API growth is guided at least 12-13%, with the animal health API base near ₹400 crore growing 20%+. A new Nalgonda block adds 128 KL of approved capacity, and Vizag expansion with US approval started commercial production in July 2026.

items.title: Animal health geographic expansion
items.text: Emerging markets grew 39% and India 49% in H1 FY27, with Turkey now shipping to Europe and Mexico front-end established. Spain and Turkey manufacturing expansion is underway, supporting double-digit FY27 Europe growth guidance even in constant currency.

items.title: Merger synergies ahead
items.text: Annualized merger synergies are tracking at ₹50-60 crores accrued, with the bigger portion due in the next 12-18 months toward a total of at least ₹125-150 crores across 15-site network optimisation and procurement. Goodwill amortization of ₹25 crores per quarter ends after the next quarter, directly lifting reported PAT.

items.title: Oncology integrated build-out
items.text: An OEB-5 high-potent R&D lab was commissioned in Hyderabad, five to six high-potent APIs are filed, and a strategic oncology manufacturing tie-up makes the company fully integrated from API to dosage. First product revenue is expected in 2029, with material contribution by FY30.
